_about: The dashboard To-Do feed: a short, layman-readable daily checklist of curation work (for Sam) and engineering/pre-curation work (for Fable, the Claude session), rendered by cpl_todos.js as the 📋 To-Do button on every tab. Refreshed at every Rule-8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff (this file is the handoff distilled for the dashboard). Check-off state lives in each viewer's browser (localStorage) and resets when _as_of changes. Keep it SHORT — ≤ ~12 items; done items are deleted, not checked.
_as_of: 2026-08-12 (late) · SkyFund — the team phrase has a home on every tab, and Contracts is on the Finance phrase.
_status: Two things today. First, the team phrase. Seven tabs needed it and had nowhere to type it — they told you to go to the Team & RACI tab, unlock there, and come back, and two of them wouldn't show you anything at all until you did. There is now one lock button in the header, on every tab, and it knows which site you have selected. Along the way we found that selecting a site never actually changed which phrase was needed: any of the phrases already opened everything. Only a tab that belongs to ONE site can sensibly ask for that site's own phrase, and exactly two do — GR Priorities, which already worked that way, and Contracts. Contracts is now live on the Finance phrase: Sam changed that password himself on the new tab and gave the go-ahead, so the register asks for Finance rather than the general team password, and anyone who only has the team one sees a box to enter it. Managing the phrases is also its own tab now, since it was buried in a button most people never saw. Second, Sierra's trainer. Sam wrote three new instructions for her and all three were being silently cut off at 500 characters — one stopped in the middle of a table. Nothing warned him. The limit is now 1,500 with a counter you can watch as you type, and Sierra is already running with it. The tab itself has been rewritten in plain English with explanations on every filter and label, and clicking Triage now leads somewhere: there is a button that starts a new instruction from the question you are looking at, because marking something 'done' never changed how Sierra answers.

items.text: Now that Contracts is locked to the Finance phrase, tell whoever works the contract register what the new phrase is. Until they have it they will see a locked page — with a box to type it into, but nothing to type. Nobody else is affected; every other tab still takes the general team phrase.

A decision worth making before the Finance phrase leaves the core team: right now a site phrase opens that site's tabs PLUS everything the shared phrase opens — budget, personnel, projects, memory, MAP contacts. That is fine while everyone holding a phrase is trusted with all of it. If Finance's phrase is going to someone outside that circle, say so and we will split them properly.

Retype your three Sierra instructions from today. They were cut off at 500 characters before the fix and the missing text was never saved, so raising the limit does not bring it back. Two stop mid-sentence and one stops in the middle of a table. You now have 1,500 characters and a counter.

There are about 25 pieces of real feedback on Sierra nobody has worked through, 11 of them thumbs-down, the oldest sitting since the start of July. The tab is finally readable — this is the first time it is worth opening. Start with the thumbs-down ones that have a written comment.

Quick sanity check when you next open COBI: there should be a small 🔒 button next to the Site dropdown at the top. Click it, enter the team phrase once, and Contracts / Governance / MAP Users / Sierra Training / the MAP Queue should all open without going anywhere else first.
Free win: the Projects editor asks for an email sign-in, but the underlying table already accepts the team phrase. Offer the phrase there too — no database change needed.

Credential Reference, Unified Courses and Canonical SUBJ4 still cannot take the team phrase, and it is not an oversight: their table stamps who made each edit from the signed-in email address, and a shared phrase has no email. Widening them needs a decision from Sam about how phrase edits should be attributed.
The next real step for Sierra is letting her quote actual documents rather than only following instructions. That is the part of the training plan still unbuilt.

Careful with Sierra's instruction length limit: the same number lives in the tab and in the server function, and they must match. Changing one alone just moves the silent cut-off to the other side, and any change needs the chat function redeployed. There is a test that fails if they drift apart.
